title: DigiRL: Training In-The-Wild Device-Control Agents with Autonomous Reinforcement Learning
abstract: DigiRL is a novel autonomous RL approach for training device control agents. It fine-tunes a pre-trained VLM in two stages: offline RL and offline-to-online RL, achieving state-of-the-art performance on Android device-control tasks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine you're trying to automate tasks on your phone, like booking a flight or sending a message. You need an AI assistant that can navigate your phone's interface and make decisions. Autonomous reinforcement learning is the key to training such an assistant. We introduce DigiRL, a novel approach that enables AI agents to learn from their own experience on the device and the Internet.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: DigiRL works in two stages: offline RL and offline-to-online RL. In the first stage, we fine-tune a pre-trained VLM using existing trajectories. In the second stage, the agent engages with real-world graphical user interfaces, enhancing its performance through online RL and autonomous performance evaluations.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: We evaluate DigiRL on the Android-in-the-Wild (AitW) dataset and achieve a 49.5% absolute improvement over supervised fine-tuning with static human demonstration data. Our approach outperforms prior state-of-the-art agents, including AppAgent with GPT-4V and the 17B CogAgent.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: DigiRL enables the development of robust and reliable device-control agents that can automate day-to-day activities on digital devices. This has significant implications for improving human life and enhancing productivity.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: DigiRL introduces several key innovations, including a novel autonomous RL approach, a scalable and parallelizable Android learning environment, and an effective RL algorithm for learning in this domain.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: We provide an open-source implementation of DigiRL, allowing researchers and practitioners to experiment with our approach and develop their own device-control agents.
